correctness.rationale: The occupancy identities prove real equality of degree-two Walsh span and two-queen incidence column span. For each order 7–11 the included explicit Gaussian-elimination pivot witness has as many distinct GF(2) pivots as configurations (40,92,352,724,2680), independently recomputed using shifted attack masks and low-bit elimination; an odd integer minor guarantees real rank. The upper bound for degree one is 1+(n−1)^2 and is smaller for all five orders. At order twelve there are 14200 configurations and at most 8712 pair columns, so the real nullity is at least 5488. Every null vector has zero total mass, yielding distinct probability laws with equal pair marginals. A separate census gives 5280 occurring two-queen patterns at order eleven, minimum positive multiplicity 2. Both packed Python programs were executed, their outputs read, and the saved witness independently replayed; no inference beyond order twelve is made.

value.rationale: For the canonical finite n-queens configuration spaces, a full two-point correlation table uniquely determines every probability law through 2680 states at order eleven, even though no individual two-square event singles out a state. The next order has a rigorous loss of at least 5488 degrees of freedom, and degree-one observables are strictly insufficient at every successful order. This sharp finite-window lower-degree recovery threshold is a meaningful natural tomography invariant, not a relabeling or a mere recomputation of the classical sequence of solution counts. No broader theorem is asserted.
